assessment.mode: Provisional conditional opportunity; data and novelty not verified

gate_evidence.G1: Partial-edit studies show that whole-recording labels can hide short generated replacements; see sections 1 and 3.
gate_evidence.G2: The shared question tests learned detection of short speech segments.
gate_evidence.G3: Members train small detection heads, learning objectives or a compressed model; no paid API is required.
gate_evidence.G4: SLR52 supplies human speech, not labelled partial deepfakes. No suitable existing Sinhala edited-speech release was verified.
gate_evidence.G5: The bounded study uses existing labels and permitted controlled derivatives. It stops if new recordings or expert labels become necessary.
gate_evidence.G6: Multilingual transfer, unseen generators, editing controls and compression have close prior work; the added contribution needs validation.
gate_evidence.G7: Sections 4 and 6 specify learning and error-trade-off experiments; the viewer is only a demonstration.
gate_evidence.G8: Metrics can be defined, but Sinhala edit timestamps and speaker/source/generator records are not secured.
gate_evidence.G9: Completion depends on early access to suitable data and a working baseline.
gate_evidence.G10: Each member has a question, trained method, comparison, ablation and separate result using the same starting model.
gate_evidence.G11: The core plan uses selected data, frozen features and small heads; full large-model training is optional.
gate_evidence.G12: Reuse terms for the actual Sinhala fake data and any generated derivatives remain unresolved.
gate_evidence.G13: Failure to transfer, editing false alarms and the accuracy-versus-size trade-off remain useful results.

ratings.confidence_and_reason: Low: Similar questions are already studied; a distinct Sinhala contribution is not established.
Low: No reusable Sinhala set with labelled AI-edited segments was verified.
Low-medium: A small study could fit, but the data and first baseline must be secured early.
Medium: The plan trains detection heads, tests learning objectives and studies model compression.
Medium-low: The test plan is clear, but Sinhala labels and source-safe splits are missing.
Medium: Each member has a separate experiment using the same unchanged starting model.
Medium: A short altered phrase can matter; benefits on real calls remain untested.
Medium-low: Selected data and frozen features should fit; training and phone costs are estimates.
Medium: A file-based viewer can highlight suspected edits without live call access.

limitations: No Sinhala edited-speech dataset verified; absence in the search is not evidence none exists.
Some initial Sinhala-specific connector queries returned off-topic records; four further searches used technical task vocabulary.
Duplication instruments returned mixed-relevance leads; neighbour status was decided from primary content, not ranking.
No audio samples, gated terms, model weights, training, runtime or phone measurements obtained.
Source cards may change; all access observations are as of 2026-10-29.
New preprints provide overlap/failure evidence, not independently reproduced results.
The two reuse notices for PartialSpoof and its underlying ASVspoof source must both be retained.
verdict: Adjust before proceeding; 62.0/100 provisional, not qualified; novelty and data remain unresolved.
